statement_details.original_sql: SELECT BusinessEntityID, FORMAT(ModifiedDate, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') AS FormattedModifiedDate, DATEDIFF(YEAR, BirthDate, GETDATE()) AS Age FROM Author WHERE DATEPART(YEAR, HireDate) = @HireDate;
statement_details.converted_sql: SELECT businessentityid, TO_CHAR(ModifiedDate, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') AS formattedmodifieddate, aws_sqlserver_ext.datediff('year', (BirthDate)::TIMESTAMP, (clock_timestamp())::TIMESTAMP) AS age FROM Author WHERE date_part('year', HireDate) = @HireDate;
statement_details.analysis: DMS converted SQL Server specific functions to PostgreSQL equivalents: FORMAT() -> TO_CHAR(), DATEDIFF() -> aws_sqlserver_ext.datediff(), DATEPART() -> date_part(), GETDATE() -> clock_timestamp(). Column names converted to lowercase per PostgreSQL conventions. Requires aws_sqlserver_ext extension.
statement_details.notes: Functionally equivalent. Requires aws_sqlserver_ext extension to be installed in PostgreSQL database for datediff function.
